title: Terms of an Approved Hold — Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
These terms govern the approval of a hold under Hardship and Protective Holds and what changes on the held account while the hold runs.

## 1. Approval

1.1 A hold that requires documentation is approved only when a record of documentation received, of the tier's documentation kind, is on record for the request. This is read from the hold request's own history before approval; the consumer's word that documents were sent does not take the place of that record.

1.2 The request is decided within the tier's decision time in business days after complete documentation arrives, or after the request where none is required.

## 2. Start and end of the hold

2.1 The hold's start date is the decision date where the tier's hold start basis is the decision date, and the request date where it is the request date.

2.2 Its end date is the start date plus the tier's initial hold days, less 1, so that the hold covers exactly the initial hold days in calendar days, the start date included.

**Worked examples (hypothetical dates, a year that is not a leap year).**

| Tier | Start basis | Request date | Decision date | Initial hold days | Start date | End date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Documented Hardship Hold | Decision date | 20 February | 4 March | 60 | 4 March | 2 May |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | Request date | 10 January | 15 January | 120 | 10 January | 9 May |

In the first row, 4 March plus 60 days less 1 is 2 May, and 4 March through 2 May is 60 calendar days. In the second, the hold starts on the request date, 10 January, and 10 January through 9 May is 120 calendar days.

## 3. While the hold runs

3.1 Outbound collection calls stop where the tier stops outbound calls; collection letters stop where the tier stops collection letters; collection emails and texts stop where the tier stops emails and text messages; no initial tradeline is furnished where the tier suspends new credit reporting; and an account with a live tradeline receives the disaster special comment where the tier's tradeline treatment is the disaster special comment.

3.2 Letters the consumer asks for, dispute verifications and the decision and end-of-hold notices are always sent.

3.3 Payments the consumer initiates are accepted where the tier accepts them, and a payment never ends the hold by itself.

## 4. Notices of the decision

4.1 Where the tier requires the client to be told of an approval, the client is notified within the tier's client notification time in business days after approval.

4.2 The decision letter is sent within the tier's decision letter time in business days after the decision.

## Questions on these terms

**Does a payment made during the hold bring it to an end?** No. Payments the consumer initiates are accepted where the tier accepts them, and a payment never ends the hold by itself.

**Will the consumer still receive mail while letters are paused?** Letters the consumer asks for, dispute verifications and the decision and end-of-hold notices are always sent, whichever activities the tier pauses.

**Can a documented tier be approved on the strength of a phone call?** Not where the tier requires documentation: approval needs a record of documentation received of the tier's kind for that request.
